headline: Large User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and certain distribution infrastructure to large energy users, primarily data centers, to reduce residential electricity bills.
status: Last Action: Governor's Action Deadline 11:59 p.m., May 23, 2026 on 2026-04-22
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocates, Dominion Energy (original bill).
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers
news_summary: Governor Spanberger suggested changes to HB 1393 and SB 253, which aimed to shift costs of new distribution infrastructure and capacity auction prices onto high-load energy users like data centers. While the original bills sought to save residential customers money and expand a power line burial program, critics argue the governor's amendments weaken these goals, particularly by removing a direct cost shift for PJM capacity costs and giving the SCC more discretion.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water users supplying data centers report their monthly or quarterly water consumption to the State Water Control Board, including reclaimed water, to increase transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental advocates (e.g., Piedmont Environmental Council), local residents, transparency advocates.
opponents: Data center industry (potential opposition due to reporting burden, but not explicitly stated as strong opposition).
news_headline: Virginia passes data center water consumption reporting bill
news_summary: SB 553 requires water users supplying data centers to report monthly or quarterly water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board. This legislation aims to provide transparency on data center water usage, a growing concern among residents and environmental advocates.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes new permit requirements for high-energy use data centers, mandating site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, environmental advocates (e.g., Piedmont Environmental Council), local government officials.
opponents: Data center industry (potential opposition due to increased regulatory burden and siting restrictions).
news_headline: Virginia enacts data center siting, noise assessment requirements
news_summary: HB 153 (identical to SB 94) establishes a new permit process for high-energy use facilities (100 MW+), requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools. Localities can also mandate assessments for impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources, reflecting growing concerns over data center development.
